Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Finova - Decision criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Emily —

Great to meet you and Chris on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Recap:
- Demo focused on real-time recommendations use case and the need to keep PII in a private environment.
- Primary goals: low latency for inference, predictable unit cost, and enterprise-grade security controls.

Open questions we discussed that will affect product/config choice:
1) Latency targets (p95/p99) for the production workload and example token lengths we should benchmark against.
2) Cost targets (e.g., target cost per 1M tokens or monthly infrastructure budget) to help pick hosted vs dedicated vs private.
3) Deployment preference: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
4) SLA requirements (uptime targets, support hours, incident response expectations).
5) Buying process & stakeholders: who’s the economic buyer, who owns procurement/legal/security reviews, and the expected procurement timeline.

Next steps (proposed):
- You to confirm the decision criteria answers above and introduce procurement/legal contacts.
- We’ll share: SOC 2 summary, data retention policy, SLA wording, and a MAP (mutual action plan) template for procurement.
- Schedule a 30–45 minute meeting next week with procurement + legal to walk through security and contract ask list.

I attached a MAP template (Finova-MAP-template.xlsx) to speed coordination. If you can share the names/emails for the procurement and legal reviewers (or loop them into this thread), I’ll get the right Redwood folks on the invite (including our lead solutions engineer, Vivek).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Mobile: (415) 555-0193

Attachment: Finova-MAP-template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finova.com>

Cc: Chris Patel <chris.patel@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — really appreciated the demo. Answering your questions below and adding a few notes on our internal process so you know what to expect.

Decision criteria (high level):
- Latency: target p95 <= 150ms for typical inference requests (~512 tokens). For some realtime widgets we’d like p99 <= 250ms.
- Cost: target runs in our modeling is ~ $2k–$5k/month for inference infra initially; we think success would be < $0.005 per 1k tokens in production (this is a rough target to inform tradeoffs).
- Deployment: preference is Dedicated (private VPC) so we can control network egress and data residency.
- SLA: minimum 99.9% monthly uptime with 24x5 support and 2–4 hour P1 response/incidence acknowledgement.

Procurement & stakeholders:
- Economic buyer: Chris Patel, CTO (cc’d).
- Procurement lead: Rajiv Menon (I’ll loop him in) — handles vendor contracts and procurement timeline.
- Legal: Nicole Alvarez — will own contract redlines and data processing terms.
- Security reviewer: internal security team will need our SOC 2 report and answers to a short questionnaire.

Timeline: procurement + security review typically takes 6–8 weeks after we kick it off; budget decision targeted for end of Q2 / start of Q3.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire and will loop Rajiv and Nicole on the follow-up meeting invite. Please include the SOC2 summary and an SLA doc in your next email.

Emily
Emily Chen
VP Product, Finova
emily.chen@finova.com

Attachment: Finova-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx stub)

Subject: Re: Finova - Decision criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Thanks Emily — that’s super helpful and gives us a clear north star for configuration and pricing.

Short answers & attachments (see attached SOC2 summary and MAP):
- Latency: we can target p95 <= 150ms on a Dedicated private VPC for your 512-token profile using our standard model profile (we’ll validate during the pilot). For p99 targets we typically provide staged SLAs and runbook options — we’ll document expected p99 numbers for your baseline model in the pilot plan.
- Cost: we’ll produce a few consumption scenarios based on your 3–5k/month starting budget and work backwards to optimize batching/quantization to hit unit economics.
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved capacity) + private VPC is supported — we’ll include configuration options (single-tenant pools vs shared reserved) in the MAP.
- SLA: Redwood offers 99.9% by default for Dedicated with optional 99.95% for enterprise tiers (with corresponding pricing). Standard response: 24x5; P1 acknowledgement within 2 hours, full incident updates per our incident playbook.

Requested items included in the attachments and links:
- SOC 2 summary (SOC2_summary.pdf) — public summary and next steps to obtain the Type II report under NDA.
- Data retention and encryption notes (link in related_links).
- Draft MAP (attached).

Next step: I’ll propose two times for a 30–45 minute meeting next week for a triage with Rajiv + Nicole to review the security questionnaire and contract touchpoints. Vivek will cover technical benchmark expectations. Does Tuesday 20 Apr 10:00–10:45 PT or Wednesday 21 Apr 14:00–14:45 PT work for you and the procurement team?
